title: Submitting needs every required acknowledgement, listed as outstanding
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in as a technician with 'Work order lines - Create & Edit', on the build under test.
  2. A filled inspection with an unacknowledged required follow-up and other missing answers/notes.
custom_steps:
1. With a required follow-up left unacknowledged, press submit and confirm the inspection cannot be submitted. (Proving the server itself refuses a submit made without the interface is a developer/automated check, not a manual step.)
2. Confirm the unacknowledged required follow-up appears in the outstanding items list alongside missing answers and notes, naming the kind first then the section, the field and the verdict, coloured by the verdict that caused it.
3. Press submit with items outstanding and confirm the list opens rather than an error dialog. Confirm Submit is never disabled, it is named 'Submit & Generate Report' on desktop and on the phone, and the list is titled 'N items before submitting', with N the number of items listed.
4. Confirm an unacknowledged follow-up does not block the action that completes a section — the count on that action rises and you may move on.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • An unacknowledged required follow-up blocks submit.
  • The block is enforced by the server: a submit made without the acknowledgement is refused whatever the interface showed.
  • An unacknowledged required follow-up appears in the outstanding items list alongside missing answers and notes, naming the kind first and then the section, the field and the verdict, and coloured by the verdict that caused it.
  • Pressing submit with items outstanding opens that list rather than raising an error dialog.
  • Submit is never disabled. It is named 'Submit & Generate Report' on every surface, and the list is titled 'N items before submitting'.
  • An unacknowledged follow-up does not block the action that completes a section; the count on that action rises and the technician may move on.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-8181, story SV-10243 (S19 — Conditional follow-up on a checkbox response); Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, section S19; read on 22 September 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S19-R22: “An unacknowledged required follow-up will block submit”
  • S19-R23: “The block will be enforced by the server. A submit made without the acknowledgement is refused whatever the interface showed”
  • S19-R24: “An unacknowledged required follow-up will appear in the outstanding items list alongside missing answers and missing notes, naming the kind first and then the section, the field and the verdict, and coloured by the verdict that caused it”
  • S19-R25: “Pressing submit with items outstanding will open that list rather than raising an error dialog. Submit is never disabled. It is named 'Submit & Generate Report' on every surface, and the list is titled 'N items before submitting'. The rule covers the submit button only; the sign-off step keeps its current labels ('Sign & generate report', 'Sign to complete', 'Confirm & lock inspection')”
  • S19-R26: “An unacknowledged follow-up will not block the action that completes a section. The count on that action rises and the technician may move on, per S14-R6”

Amended on 12 October 2026
The S19-R25 quote above now carries the whole rule (Digital Inspections V2 specification, Confluence page 768507905, version 42 of 7 October 2026, read on 12 October 2026); before, it stopped after the first sentence. Step 3 and the expected results now also check that Submit is never disabled, its name and the list title. The sign-off step's labels are outside this case.

Last checked against build v26.36.8-2a64085 on 10/1/2026.
